open_points.subject: reopened decision range
open_points.text: the owner's answers of 2026-10-27 on its conflicts with that frame are recorded as R0-24 to R0-60
open_points.question: Are the accepted R0-61 to R0-67 decisions also part of the reopened frame, and should the stated range include them?
options: Extend the range through R0-67
Treat R0-61 to R0-67 as outside the reopened frame

open_points.subject: optional project customer
open_points.text: It says which projects exist, which customer each is for
open_points.question: May a project have no customer as R0-16 says, or must every project identify a customer?
options: A project may have no customer
Every project must have a customer
open_points.default_guess: A project may have no customer.

open_points.subject: one-project-one-object invariant after anonymisation
open_points.text: A project has exactly one object
open_points.question: Does this invariant exclude anonymised projects, which R0-60 and R0-62 say retain no object?
options: The invariant applies only before anonymisation
An anonymised project must retain a non-identifying object shell
open_points.default_guess: The invariant applies only to projects that have not been anonymised.

open_points.subject: Kernel output boundary
open_points.text: receives only what K-14 lets through
open_points.question: What concrete output filtering or disclosure guarantee does K-14 provide, given that K-14 is not defined in this text?
options: Restate the required K-14 guarantee here
Remove K-14 as a source of Registry behavior
Make K-14 an explicitly carried external contract
open_points.default_guess: Restate here that Kernel passes only the declared agent-authority output projection.

open_points.subject: personal values in agent-visible free-form fields
open_points.text: sees each through a minimal projection without personal values
open_points.question: How is the no-personal-values guarantee preserved when agent-visible display names, room names, artifact URIs, payload references or digests can themselves contain identifying information?
options: Constrain and refuse personal values in agent-visible fields
Omit or redact affected fields from agent outputs
Define these fields as never personal regardless of their contents
open_points.default_guess: Constrain inputs and omit any pointer fields whose values are not guaranteed non-personal from agent outputs.

open_points.subject: audit subject identifiers
open_points.question: How can an audit entry identify the affected project or customer while carrying no personal value, when a project identity is explicitly not anonymous by itself and a customer reference may identify a person?
options: Store opaque non-identifying audit subject handles
Allow identifiers in the audit log and classify them accordingly
Record only subject type without an identifier
open_points.default_guess: Use an opaque audit subject handle that is not returned outside the owner-only audit view.

open_points.subject: audited state changes
open_points.text: Registry records only significant changes of state: changes to projects and customer records, granting and revoking an agent session's projects, restricting processing and lifting it, and erasures and anonymisations.
open_points.question: Exactly which new actions are significant and audited—for example room creation, artifact publication or withdrawal, session registration, active-project changes, access requests and answers, imports, relationship end or resume, and audit-log erasure?
options: Declare an exhaustive audited-action list
Audit every state-changing primary action
Audit only the examples currently named
open_points.default_guess: Audit every state-changing primary action except pending access requests, and explicitly enumerate the exceptions.

open_points.subject: revision preconditions across owner actions
open_points.text: Every change carries CSRF protection and is validated on the server; a change made against an older revision is refused
open_points.question: Which owner changes require which revision, given that only projects and customers have record revisions while session access, imports and the audit log also have owner changes?
options: Require revisions only for project and customer changes
Use the session access version for session mutations and define concurrency tokens for other mutable aggregates
Require no stale-write check for actions without a declared revision
open_points.default_guess: Use project/customer revisions for those records, the access version for session mutations, and explicit operation-specific concurrency rules for imports and audit erasure.

open_points.subject: session access version
open_points.question: What changes the access version, and must grant, revoke, active-project change, request replacement and request answer state the version they were made against?
options: Increment it for every change to grants, active project or pending request and require it on mutations
Increment it only for grant and active-project changes
Expose it as informational without stale-write enforcement
open_points.default_guess: Increment it for every mutation of the session access record and require it on owner mutations.

open_points.subject: agent operation without an active project
open_points.text: at most one active project, the default when the agent names none
open_points.question: What happens when an agent-authority project operation supplies no project id and the session has no active project?
options: Refuse with a non-enumerating no-active-project failure
Require every call to name a granted project
Choose a project from the granted set automatically
open_points.default_guess: Refuse with a generic no-active-project failure that reveals nothing about other projects.

open_points.subject: unregistered session refusal
open_points.text: a session that is not registered refused like a call outside the set
open_points.question: What observable refusal is returned for an unregistered session on access reads or free-text access requests, which have no project id and therefore cannot literally look like an outside-set project call?
options: Use one generic unavailable-or-not-authorized refusal for both cases
Return session-not-found
Return project-not-found despite there being no project input
open_points.default_guess: Use a generic unavailable-or-not-authorized refusal shared by unregistered and unauthorized agent-authority calls.

open_points.subject: rooms of an anonymised project
open_points.text: An anonymised project keeps its id, status and artifact pointers and nothing else.
open_points.question: What does list rooms return for an anonymised project whose id still exists but whose rooms were removed?
options: Answer that the project was erased
Return an empty room list
Refuse as not found
open_points.default_guess: Answer that the project was erased, matching read project, context and agent projection.

open_points.subject: granting while answering an access request
open_points.text: granting adds the project the owner picks from the catalogue to the session's set
open_points.question: What happens if the selected project is unknown, archived, anonymised, deleted or already granted when the owner answers the request?
options: Apply the same failures and idempotency as the standalone grant action
Clear the request but make no grant
Refuse the whole answer and leave the request pending
open_points.default_guess: Apply the standalone grant rules; on failure leave the request pending.

open_points.subject: repeated customer-state transitions
open_points.text: restrict or lift a restriction on a customer
open_points.question: What happens when the owner restricts an already restricted customer or lifts a restriction that is not present?
options: Return the customer unchanged
Refuse the invalid transition
Record another revision despite no state change
open_points.default_guess: Return the customer unchanged without moving its revision.

open_points.subject: repeated relationship-state transitions
open_points.text: end or resume a customer relationship
open_points.question: What happens when the owner ends an already ended relationship, resumes one that is not ended, or supplies a different end date for an already ended relationship?
options: Treat equal repeats as unchanged and require correction for a different date
Refuse every transition that does not change the state
Overwrite the existing end date
open_points.default_guess: Return equal repeats unchanged, refuse resume when not ended, and treat a changed end date as an explicit correction.

open_points.subject: repeated session grants and active-project changes
open_points.text: the project joins the session's granted set; the owner may also make it the session's active project
open_points.question: What happens when the project is already granted, is already active, or is granted again with a request to make it active?
options: Use set semantics and return the resulting access unchanged where nothing changes
Refuse duplicate grants and no-op active changes
Always move the access version even when state is unchanged
open_points.default_guess: Use idempotent set semantics and do not move the access version when nothing changes.

open_points.subject: clearing or selecting an active project
open_points.question: Does this action explicitly allow clearing the active project, and may an archived but still granted project be selected as active?
options: Allow clearing; require a selected active project to be active
Allow clearing and allow archived projects to remain or become active-but-inactive contexts
Do not allow explicit clearing
open_points.default_guess: Allow clearing, but refuse selecting an archived or erased project as active.

open_points.subject: imported record state
open_points.text: the projects of that source under the identities they carry, with their customers (`customer_ref` kept), objects, rooms and pointers (ids kept), links intact
open_points.question: Which non-identity state is preserved or initialized during import—project and pointer statuses, revisions, timestamps, customer erased/restricted/ended marks, archive dates and artifact version history?
options: Preserve every supported source state and initialize fields absent from the old source by declared migration defaults
Import only the listed identity graph and initialize all other state
Refuse exports that cannot supply every current field
open_points.default_guess: Preserve supported historical state and define explicit defaults for fields that did not exist in the source version.

open_points.subject: audit cutoff date
open_points.text: every entry older than the date the owner gives is gone; the erasure leaves an entry of its own naming the date
open_points.question: May the owner give a future date, which would make the newly written erasure entry itself older than the cutoff while the promised output says it remains?
options: Refuse a cutoff later than the operation time
Evaluate deletion before appending the erasure entry even for a future cutoff
Allow the new entry to violate the cutoff postcondition
open_points.default_guess: Refuse a cutoff later than the current time.
